form_analysis.feedback: Appropriate aftercare for a light, 'lunchtime' peel. Emphasises the subtle nature of the treatment while still enforcing core chemical peel principles (sun care, no picking). Good for managing patient expectations of minimal flaking.

form_data.introduction: This aftercare advice is for a light chemical peel targeting the very top layer of skin (stratum corneum). Recovery is quick, but proper care ensures optimal brightening and smoothing results.

instructions.general_directive: Please follow the General Chemical Peel Principles, with the following specific notes for your superficial peel.

sections.title: Immediate Post-Treatment Symptoms and Timeline
sections.content: You may experience a mild tingling or warmth for up to 20 minutes post-peel. Skin will appear slightly pink or shiny for 1-12 hours. Very light, sandpaper-like flaking or subtle peeling may occur on days 2-3, often barely visible. Your skin may feel tight.

sections.title: Specific Instructions
items: Peeling/Frosting: You likely will not have visible 'sheets' of peeling skin. Flaking may be so light it comes off during cleansing.
Cleansing/Moisturizing: You may cleanse gently 4-6 hours post-peel. Apply a light, non-comedogenic moisturizer as needed for tightness.
Sun Protection: ABSOLUTELY CRITICAL. Even though visible damage is minimal, UV exposure post-peel can trigger pigmentation. Apply SPF 30+ daily.
Product Restart: You may be able to resume your regular active products (like retinol or AHAs) after 3-5 days, or as instructed.

sections.title: Activity Restrictions
sections.content: Avoid strenuous exercise and excessive heat for 24 hours. You may resume normal activities almost immediately.

sections.title: Makeup
sections.content: You can typically apply makeup within a few hours, once any tingling has stopped and the skin feels normal.

sections.title: General Side Effects and Results Assessment
items: Adverse reactions are rare. Contact your practitioner if you experience significant redness, swelling, blistering, or itching beyond 24 hours.
Results are subtle: a fresher, more radiant complexion with improved texture. Multiple treatments (4-6 spaced 2-4 weeks apart) yield the best outcome.
This is a maintenance treatment, not a one-time correction.

patient_declaration.question_opportunity: Please let your practitioner know if you have any questions or if you do not understand any of the aftercare instructions provided below.

recommendations: Remind patients that even though it's 'light,' sun protection is non-negotiable for preventing complications.
